answer: A ballot grazes a meadow and leaves a trail behind it. Each job is stamped in ferrous ink on a public mirror log; each tide, a random peer replays one entry and checks the reflection. Clone farms die by the mirror check: ten ballots replaying the same ten jobs in the same order burn together, stakes slashed. Carnegie Mellon had 51 typists type one password 400 times and told them apart with 9.6% error, so 10,000 fake trails need 10,000 distinct rhythms and 400,000 grazing hours, with a $25 bond per ballot — $250,000 locked away. A meadow remembers every grazer; each fake hoofprint is $25.
